issues.title: Next AQUORA P0: All three visualizers must respond strongly to internal music even when physical master volume is zero
issues.body:
## Owner physical FM-1 request — Nov 7, 2026 — all modes, including master level zero

> "all visualizer should react much more to the audio, and even [if] the volume is set to 0."

This is an explicit **cross-mode** requirement: **Original** (Mode 1), preserved **Cymatics** (Mode 2) and planned **Chladni** (Mode 3, #36) must show substantially clearer, musically meaningful motion. **Turning the FM-1's physical master volume knob all the way to zero must NOT stop or suppress visualization while the AQUORA transport/audio engine is still producing music internally.** Visually silent != acoustically muted.

### Exact audio signal contract (avoid false triggers)
- Drive visual animation using **internal pre-physical-master / pre-speaker-output** signal telemetry: audio energy / RMS, transient/onset strength, per-role audible contributions, harmonic/pitch context and optional spectral proxies from the engine **before hardware master attenuation**. Preserve proper **post-track/solo/arrangement-gain** semantics: a muted or inactive role should not create fictitious "audible" visual peaks; external audio if actually routed through engine can be included when available. Effective internal mix can still animate while headphone/speaker output is muted.
- Physical master **0% vs 100%** for the same sequence should yield **equivalent visual motion** (apart from nondeterministic capture timing), despite exactly muted DAC output at 0%. This behavior should also hold during smooth changes of master while running and after saved preferences reload.
- No "visualization from the absolute constant animation clock only": rhythmic kicks should induce conspicuous but controlled impulses, bass should cause slower/heavier waves, melody pitches should affect motion/geometry, chords should generate coherent interference; quiet passages should be visibly calmer, and attack/decay should be observable. Keep the artistically distinct identities of the three modes.
- When **STOP** is pressed or engine genuinely silent, visual activity should **decay/settle naturally**, not keep showing full-volume musical excitation. Intentional reference/binaural/Nature layers may animate only when truly active internally. Preserve ongoing ambient ease; avoid frantic strobing / flicker and false “frequency healing” claims.
- Respect user-selected black/white background and improved white-theme contrast requirement #37. Preserve particularly the current **Cymatics Mode 2** black-background appearance, not replace it with Mode 3's nodal mandalas.
- Avoid additional DSP/heavy analysis in the real-time audio callback. Reuse existing pre-master track meters, `engine.master_peak`, role/onset/pitch telemetry as safe inputs or add lightweight bounded snapshots; use frame-domain smoothing/attack-release and separate geometry/render work, not FFT or costly sample-by-sample graphics.

### Current source grounding (v0.6.6)
- `device/app.c::app_render(...,master)` applies physical master in `output_gain` **after** `sr_render(&engine,pcm,n)`. The internal mix/telemetry therefore need not be tied to hardware master, but must be verified through end-to-end tests.
- `device/visual_worker.c::prepare_geometry()` samples `engine.tracks[t].meter`, role onset/events, pitch and engine frequency; `visual_job` uses meter to set Original petal radius and `resonance_job` uses meter/onset to drive Cymatics water/sand. They may need **higher perceptual dynamic range**, more transient response and more meaningful musical differentiation without driving overload.
- Do not fake a full audio response simply by cranking up static `energy` or decorative phase, nor derive visual amplitude from the post-hardware-master `lr[]` output buffer.

### Acceptance criteria and evidence
1. Deterministic/recorded **same internally generated musical sequence** at physical master 0, low, and high: output PCM muted at zero, yet per-frame visual telemetry and geometric reaction demonstrably equivalent. Also move master dynamically during PLAY; no discontinuity in visual response.
2. Contrast clips: kick/snare/percussion transients, solo bass swell/glide, lead notes, chord/polyphony, changing pitch & harmonies, loud-vs-soft, Nature-only, intentional silence, STOP and release tails. Every mode must show strong **observable correlations to music** and reasonable decay; no permanently animated noisy screen while truly stopped.
3. Validate all three modes in black/white themes and full-screen/PLAY; 240×240 genuine renderer captures/short animations for comparison, owner aesthetic approval pending physical device test.
4. Keep v0.6.6 smoothness and audio-first priority: host/native/forced-single-core tests, instrument frame p95/p99, FPS/XRUN safety, DMA ownership; robust fallback if load high. No additional full-screen redraw per sample, preserve battery and display responsiveness.
5. Record required traceability in #32 matrix and active queue; **this is new post-v0.6.6 scope**. Preserve published release/tag/installer; do not restart an active build, do not modify KIRA-9; USB/BLE performance MIDI remain owner-authorized deferred.

## Owner scope revision — 2026-11-07 (supersedes earlier "improve/replace Cymatics Mode 2" interpretation)

**KEEP the existing v0.6.6 second visualizer, _Cymatics_, exactly as a selectable mode.** Owner likes its appearance, **especially on a black background**, and does **not** want its artistic identity replaced by Chladni/mandala patterns. 2. **Cymatics** — preserve the current v0.6.6 water/sand mode and particularly its black-background appearance, existing water feel and smoothness. Any shared improvements must be non-destructive and independently reviewed.
3. **NEW: Chladni** — visually distinct, explicitly music-reactive vibrating-plate/sand nodal figures and elegant geometric/mandala-like forms.

- **True audible post-gain reactivity:** energetic transient response (including audible drums), pitch/harmonics influencing modal geometry, bass swelling and release, meaningful loud/quiet differences; avoid decorative random animation disconnected from sound.

No scientific-fidelity or mystical-frequency claims.

Include fullscreen/idle startup settings, visualizer persistence, host controls, emulator and website parity. Prevent changing source mode by unrelated controls.

Test all three modes, selection/persistence/migration, audio-first FPS/XRUN, delayed-DMA and single-core fallback. This is **new post-v0.6.6 scope**. Preserve existing published v0.6.6 packages, tests, repositories and installers; no unapproved code edits or parallel builders. Both USB and BLE performance MIDI remain explicitly deferred; KIRA-9 untouched.

issues.body:
## Owner physical FM-1 feedback — post-v0.6.6 (2026-11-07)

**Observed:** The new v0.6.6 firmware is very smooth. On the SOUND page, rotating the **SELECT encoder** appears to do *something*, but the owner cannot tell what, and can no longer reliably cycle/identify the different musical tracks. In particular, the owner cannot select **Lead** or **Bass** to set glide and vibrato. This was reachable in prior behavior. Treat as **P0 UI / parameter-access regression**, not hardware failure.

### Source clues to reproduce and verify (do not assume tested behavior)
- `device/app.c::app_input_only` `enc[1]` (EN_SELECT) falls back to `selected=bounded(selected+d,0,7)` on SOUND, but `sound_picker` is never assigned `1` in current `device/app.c` (only tested or reset to 0). There is likely unreachable, stale selector UI.
- `device/ui.c` prints `role_names[selected]` prominently in SOUND **group==0**, while other SOUND tabs (notably MOTION group==6) show group title/levels, with no obvious permanent `LEAD/BASS` active-role indicator.
- `device/app.c` binds **press SEL** on SOUND to `send(15,0)` (mute toggle), whereas **turn SELECT** should move role. Preserve meaningful safe semantics and label these separately. Check whether a press is being mistaken for role selection or causing unintentional mute.
- `device/app.c` MOTION controls map group 6 K1..K4 to `glide_mode`, `glide_ms`, `vibrato_rate`, `vibrato_depth` but their actual target is `c.track=selected`. Values only apply for selected <= SR_BASS. `device/ui.c` says "Use SELECT knob" when out of range, without showing currently selected track.

### Required correction
1. Restore intuitive, deterministic **turn SELECT → select Track** across all SOUND sections; clearly show the current track name and selection changes on screen, including MOTION. No hidden, silent action.

4. Persistent compact contextual control hints, role label, live knob values; do not sacrifice UI readability or render/audio performance. Distinguish **turn SELECT** versus **press SEL**.
5. Add focused **actual firmware input-path / host encoder simulation** acceptance (lead→bass→other roles, each SOUND subpage, MOTION editing/readback, mute/sound-lock, SAVE/reload, reverse direction / bounds) plus small on-screen preview evidence; preserve v0.6.6 stability and low FPS/XRUN overhead.

**Release disposition:** Carry forward as required **next corrective release**. v0.6.6 is already published, so do not edit/tag/publish over it or claim its physical acceptance passed. issues.title: P0 next build: eight-role arrangement evolution, fading entrances/exits and inactive mixer tracks
issues.body:
## Owner-reported hardware observation — November 6, 2026

While watching the MIXER on the latest AQUORA firmware, the owner sees that **all eight tracks never seem to be used**: some tracks appear disabled, unassigned, or never generate audio over the entire listening period. This is an observational report, **not yet a verified root cause**. The latest build otherwise runs smoothly with no lag observed so far; protect that performance baseline.

## Required next-build investigation and fix

1. Audit the **eight intended musical roles, including drums**, their patch/kit assignment, generated phrases and evolution, and mixer track/bus mapping. Confirm whether all eight are configured, enabled, and capable of contributing in the default arrangement. Distinguish genuinely silent source roles from non-role buses and intentionally sparse musical rests.
2. Trace each role across generator selection -> note scheduling -> voices/voice stealing -> envelopes/FX -> gains/mute/solo/Auto Level/Auto Gain -> mixer meters -> DAC. Look for permanently empty/unassigned patches, zero gain, mute defaults, routing/channel mismatches, low priority voices, and UI meters that falsely imply inactivity.
3. Exercise **13 intentions × three music modes**, and **16/32/64** step loops, New Song, Reroll Sounds, Freeze/evolution, save/recall, STOP/PLAY, and intentional sparse arrangements. Ensure each role expected by the design becomes meaningfully active over a long enough interval, with musical variation and without mandatory eight-part continuous playback.
4. Add targeted role-activity diagnostics: per-role patch ID, enabled/mute/solo state, generated-event count, accepted voice count, post-gain signal level/peak and mixer meter identity. In automated renders, inspect both event counts and actual audible PCM per-role stems / sampled mix; distinguish silence caused by intentional arrangement from failure.
5. Fix proven defects **without** forcing all eight roles to sound in every bar, muddying arrangements, artificially inflating meters, increasing CPU/XRUNs, or regressing the owner's currently smooth v0.6.5 audio/UI performance.
6. Supply source+test evidence and before/after diagnostics, plus a short owner hardware acceptance checklist showing how to verify all eight roles on the FM-1 mixer. Mark physical confirmation **OWNER-UNVERIFIED** until tested.

**Priority:** P0 core generative audio role/track integrity for next build. Carry forward in `NEXT_BUILD_ACTIVE.md` and requirement matrix Issue #32. Do not modify published v0.6.5 assets as part of this backlog note.

## Additional owner hardware feedback — dynamic track entrances/exits (2026-11-06)

Owner clarification: a generated song **typically uses the same ~4–5 musical tracks for the entire listening session**; those parts persist, while remaining roles stay silent from start to finish. The desired experience is a living arrangement: **different roles should gradually enter and leave as the song evolves**, with audible, smooth fade-ins and fade-outs rather than a fixed set of channels throughout the song.

### Acceptance criteria (added to existing P0 issue)

- Implement or verify a phrase-/section-level **role-activity plan** for all eight intended musical roles (including drums): rotate supporting parts in/out over time while retaining harmonic coherence, intention/style, recognizability and musical flow. Evolution should be perceptible across **16/32/64-step loops** and longer sessions.
- Support smoothly automated **per-role fade-in/fade-out envelopes** and appropriate transitions/crossfades on phrase or section boundaries (click-free, avoid abrupt re-entry, note tails/reverb handled gracefully); protect the audio-thread budget. Preserve musical rests and occasional intentionally sparse passages; **do not force eight simultaneous loud tracks**.
- Check whether silent roles result from generator assignment or eligibility, missing phrase triggers, role activation state, instrument selection, signal routing, or mixer metering; ensure that **each enabled, eligible role has a realistic opportunity to become audible during evolution**, not only when restarting or manually changing intentions. A permanently silent role should be explicable by a user mute/lock/intentional arrangement rule, not accidental omission.
- Verify gradual entrances and exits are reflected accurately in the MIXER: role meters track real post-gain signal and controls remain intuitive; no fake audio or artificially animated meters.
- Add extended deterministic scenario tests and per-role stem/meter timelines for 13 intentions × three modes, 16/32/64 steps, New Song/Reroll/Freeze, plus save/recall. Assert meaningful **variation in active-role sets** and transitions over a realistic multi-evolution duration, not merely a nonzero note for each track. Exclude deliberately frozen, soloed or muted roles from inappropriate assertions.
- Measure fade slopes, clicks, audible onset/decay, XRUN, CPU and visual responsiveness against v0.6.5; preserve the owner's current **no-lag** observation. Include explicit **OWNER-HARDWARE-UNVERIFIED** listening/mixer checks in the final acceptance notes.

This is a **requested next-build behavior**, not an implemented fix or evidence that the current generator is broken in a particular subsystem. Do not start a separate concurrent build or modify the current released firmware for this note.


## Owner clarification — musical discretion, not eight-track quota

All eight roles are **available**, but **they do not all need to play in the same song, at once, or even during one entire song**. The style, selected intention, chord/harmonic progression, musical phrases and evolving arrangement should organically determine which instruments enter, overlap, fade, depart, or remain silent. A beautiful sparse piece might use only a few. Some styles or evolutions may genuinely call for all eight. The failure to investigate is **permanently unavailable/nonfunctional roles or an unintentionally static 4–5-track configuration**, not a requirement to force every role into every composition. No arbitrary minimum-track quota or rotation timer. Test all eight roles' capability in suitable contexts and the musical appropriateness of transitions.

## Comparative engine review (2026-11-06)
Reviewed actual [SIREN 0.9.1 source](https://github.com/isod89/siren-fm1) and AQUORA's `device/dsp/engine.c`. The actionable original-design handoff is [validation/SIREN_GENERATIVE_ENGINE_REVIEW_2026-11-06.md](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/blob/main/validation/SIREN_GENERATIVE_ENGINE_REVIEW_2026-11-06.md). Prioritize section-level role planning with intention/music-mode/harmonic context, optional gradual role fade entrances/exits, stable motif return, deterministic seeds and true post-gain audio/stem checks. SIREN demonstrates style-weighted forms and section-aware note gating; its code does **not** demonstrate the desired continuous eight-role crossfade system, which AQUORA must design independently. Respect SIREN's GPL-3.0-only copyright conditions; do not copy source/tables/assets without distribution-license review. Research only, no firmware implementation or release claim.

issues.body:
# User-approved requirement — next AQUORA build (after v0.6.5)
**Goal (updated Nov 5, 2026):** AQUORA and KIRA-9 are the **only two active firmware projects**. Implement a **generic, standards-compatible MIDI subsystem** in both, with **direct wireless BLE MIDI** and **USB MIDI through an optional iPad USB hub/CoreMIDI router** (e.g. midimittr). Direct FM-1-to-FM-1 TRS MIDI cabling remains out of scope. Both paths shall work with any standards-compliant compatible peer, no hardcoded KIRA-9 whitelist. Preserve AQUORA's accepted v0.6.5 audio/performance/SAVE behavior.

## Reference implementations to audit (do not copy without license review)
- Baud Girl FM-1+VA version 97+ demonstrates direct FM-1 ↔ FM-1 BLE MIDI clock, **BT Host** versus **BT Device** roles, MIDI clock/Start/Stop/Continue, remembered peer, role switching/reconnect. Reference: https://baudgirl.com/work/FM-1%2BVA/announcements/version-97 and https://baudgirl.com/work/FM-1%2BVA/manual/102
- SLOOP is **not BLE-capable**; borrow protocol discipline only (24 PPQN phase tracking, transport, note-off reliability, no feedback loops, channel mapping): https://github.com/isod89/sloop-fm1/blob/main/GUIDE.md
- MIKU-FM1 is a vocal/formant FM-1 precedent, **not proof of English natural-vocal or BLE** functionality: https://github.com/MichaelAPerry/MIKU-FM1

## AQUORA release requirements
1. Survey real AQUORA SDK/BLE stack, hardware limits, current passive-radio AIR path and Bluetooth resource ownership; assess central/peripheral support and compatibility with both FM-1s before choosing a solution. Do not break AIR or the existing audio ISR to make BLE work. Document dependencies and conflicts.
2. Support standardized BLE MIDI interoperability with generic scan/discovery of **any compatible MIDI peer**, not KIRA-9-specific IDs/names; support **Host (central)**, **Device (peripheral)**, and **Off** as hardware allows. Discover standard BLE MIDI GATT service, implement BLE MIDI packet/timestamp encoding and decoding, configurable local device name, remember selected peer(s), reconnect, observable link diagnostics and safe role switching. Default demonstration: AQUORA host + KIRA-9 peripheral; allow reverse roles if technically supported. No clock or note feedback loops.
3. **Transmit** standard 24 PPQN MIDI clock (0xF8), Start (0xFA), Continue (0xFB), Stop (0xFC), configurable Always/Playing/Off; never emit own clock while slaved to an external clock. Send intended AQUORA melodic-role notes with correct Note On/Off/velocity, configurable MIDI channel and source track. Sustain, rests, tempo changes, octaves, step-length switches, key-change and Play Along must preserve notes/time; STOP and disconnect flush all active notes.
4. **Receive** BLE MIDI transport, clock, notes, CC, pitch bend and program/phrase-selection where appropriate, with optional external-clock slave mode and safe routing. Avoid MIDI echo/feedback; no duplicate or hanging notes. Document unsupported messages.
5. Define a **reusable, firmware-agnostic BLE MIDI protocol module** and a versioned optional **application profile** usable by **AQUORA and KIRA-9 today and future compatible firmware**: standard channels, clock/transport, notes/velocity/gate, bend, expression/dynamics, Program Change, song position, and optional indexed phrase/style/voice controls. Keep the core interoperable without proprietary extensions. Scope feature-specific extension handling to a negotiated/capability-detected optional layer; **never assume a peer is KIRA-9**, nor that ordinary MIDI carries arbitrary English lyrics. KIRA-9 prepares lyrics locally and can select phrase IDs via agreed MIDI messages. No Bluetooth audio streaming; both devices synthesize locally. Provide shared protocol documentation + independent conformance fixtures/tests so each project can implement it without importing the other's business logic.
6. On-device SETUP > WIRELESS/MIDI page: BT role, generic discovered peer list/name, current peer/connection status, sync clock master/slave/off, clock out mode, transmit source/channel, MIDI channel receive filters, reconnect, panic/all-notes-off, signal diagnostics. Put **KIRA-9-specific mappings** (lyric phrase/voice/style events) in a separate optional application profile, not the generic MIDI pairing UI. Show LIVE measured states (not fake "Scanning"), accessible K1-K4 values, quick-find entries, SAVE/restore.
7. **AQUORA AIR coexistence policy:** BT passive scan/proximity and active BLE MIDI may contend for radio; characterize resources and airtime. Support both only if measured safe; else make the modes explicit and mutually exclusive with on-screen explanation. Default BT Off until configured; measure CPU/audio IRQ/DMA/XRUN, packet rates, latency/jitter and battery.
8. Recovery/safety: disconnection while singing, rapid reconnects, late/missing clock, power-cycle remembered peer, role changes, dense sequences, malformed BLE packet input, transport reset/continue, tempo swings, 8-hour-equivalent stress with BLE fixtures. Guard bounded message queues and audio priority; no long blocking callbacks, no crash or permanent note latch.
9. Automated host BLE-MIDI codec/parser and scheduling tests, two-node simulated integration, emulator UI/control coverage, firmware build/package identity and checksums, GitHub Actions repeatability. **Physical FM-1↔FM-1 BLE pairing/jitter/RF/latency and AIR coexistence are OWNER HARDWARE UNVERIFIED until user tests both devices.** Include a concise physical test matrix and fallback.
10. Full end-to-end normal build/release workflow with exclusive build lock, verified GitHub checkpoints/remote backup, no repeated already-passed acceptance except changed regressions, accurate Next Build queue. Preserve released 0.6.5 and installer; publish only when software release gates pass. On failure, retain prior release and checkpoint with blocked items.



## NEW USER-APPROVED PATH: iPad USB hub / CoreMIDI routing (Nov 5, 2026)
The owner ALSO wants to connect **both active M-VAVE FM-1 devices over USB-C data cables** to a **powered USB hub attached to an iPad**, route their MIDI ports through a third-party CoreMIDI app such as **midimittr**, and run synchronized AQUORA ↔ KIRA-9 performances. This **supersedes the earlier all-wireless-only scope ONLY as to an optional iPad USB host bridge**. Direct TRS MIDI cabling between FM-1s is still out of scope. BLE direct communication remains first-class and should work without any iPad.

### Required architecture / acceptance
1. **One shared, transport-neutral MIDI event/core protocol** in each firmware. Both **BLE MIDI** and **USB class-compliant MIDI device** adapters feed the same clock/transport, note, CC, pitch bend, program change and optional versioned profile handling. No hardcoded dependency on KIRA-9 or on a specific MIDI routing app. Future compatible firmware can interoperate via standard MIDI.
2. **USB MIDI device IN + OUT**, independent ports/endpoints exposed through iPadOS **CoreMIDI**. Distinct, human-readable USB product/interface names **AQUORA** and **KIRA-9** where descriptor implementation allows, and stable endpoints/identities for routing. USB MIDI OUT is crucial: AQUORA must actually transmit clock/notes, not merely receive input from the iPad. Both devices simultaneously enumerate behind a hub. Confirm/repair current firmware USB descriptors and firmware event I/O; do not mistake successful USB firmware-update SysEx support for ordinary bidirectional performance MIDI.
3. iPadOS host connectivity: support two USB MIDI 1.0 class-compliant peripherals simultaneously, through an appropriately powered hub/data cables. Verify enumeration and visible per-device MIDI input/output in midimittr (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/midimittr/id925495245) and with an independent CoreMIDI inspector / MIDI monitor; iPad charging/power budgets and USB-C versus Lightning adapters depend on model.
4. **Routing test**: AQUORA USB MIDI Out → iPad midimittr source-to-destination route → KIRA-9 USB MIDI In. Full 24 PPQN clock, Start/Stop/Continue, melodic note-on/off, gates, velocity, song/phrase Program/CC and pitch bend, synchronized English singing and animation. For bi-directional control, configure selectively routed KIRA-9 MIDI Out → AQUORA MIDI In, with no clock/notes reflected back into the origin.
5. **Clock master policy**: select a single leader — by default AQUORA; or an iPad DAW/clock source if desired. midimittr is a **router**, not necessarily an independent clock generator; never assume it creates MIDI clock or arranges lyrics. KIRA-9 follows incoming tempo/transport and locally prepared lyric/voice presets. iPad DAW can drive both as independent recipients. Robust detection/priority when USB and BLE are connected simultaneously: explicit input preference (USB, BLE, Auto with lock), no double clock, echo, loops, orphaned notes or unsafely merged transports.
6. USB disconnect, hub brownout, app background/foreground changes, port re-enumeration, cable unplug/replug and reconnect recovery: audio engine continues safely; clear stale active notes; resync on next clock/transport; no blocked audio callback. Reuse BLE/USB-independent message parser and bounded timestamped scheduler where technically appropriate.
7. Comprehensive tests: USB descriptor enumeration fixtures, per-port in/out, simulated two-node iPad MIDI forwarding and clock jitter/latency; emulator menus/transport routing; run independent regressions; owner physical tests of **two FM-1s + iPad + powered hub + midimittr**, note/clock logs, reconnection and actual latency/jitter. Mark iPad hardware interoperability **UNVERIFIED** until physical run.
8. UI: SETTINGS > MIDI page exposes USB IN/OUT state, BLE connection, MIDI transport input precedence, clock master/slave/off, selectable source role and channels, independent ports/route status if detectable, panic and diagnostics. Do not imply firmware can detect which third-party iPad app is actively routing MIDI merely from USB enumeration. Bluetooth features still work when USB bridge isn't present.
9. Preserve prior 0.6.5 acceptance and AIR/radio policies. iPad hub operation must not require a new iPad app, custom driver, firmware flasher, or exclusive proprietary SysEx.
10. Reference evidence: Dinghy FM-1 documents class-compliant USB MIDI IN/OUT (https://github.com/zvenson/dinghy); Apple documents iPad USB hubs and MIDI devices (https://support.apple.com/en-am/108894); Apple recommends powered hubs for multiple devices (https://support.apple.com/guide/logicpro-ipad/connect-external-devices-lpip26513101/3.3/ipados/26); midimittr's App Store listing states USB/BLE MIDI routing and remembers routing settings. Its route behavior with BOTH custom firmwares still requires physical verification.

**Revised validation scenarios:** A: AQUORA↔KIRA-9 direct BLE link without iPad. B: Both FM-1s connected via powered USB hub to iPad with midimittr routing, fully synchronized. C: Generic third-party USB/ BLE MIDI peer compatibility. D: simultaneous USB+BLE connected safely with one authoritative clock.

## Acceptance scenarios
1. **Current two-project integration**: orange KIRA-9 FM-1 as BLE MIDI Device and AQUORA as Host/clock master; select remembered peer; pressing PLAY sends clock + Start and selected role melody notes; KIRA-9 follows while singing its *locally prepared* English lyrics; tempo/key changes remain synchronized; STOP and disconnect close every note; reconnect and power cycles restore pairing safely.
2. **Generic MIDI interoperability**: discover, connect and exchange standard MIDI with a BLE MIDI test peer whose name and identity **do not** contain 'KIRA' or 'AQUORA'; verify notes/transport/control, no application-profile requirement, no hidden whitelist. Where possible test against an independent standards-compliant BLE MIDI implementation, not just our own code.
3. **Future-compatible design, not extra active projects**: publish the versioned MIDI core/interface contract and conformance fixtures for potential future firmware, but do not create, resume, or spend development effort on any other firmware project. Record actual latency/jitter on physical devices as owner-unverified until tested.

**Status:** NEW / NOT IMPLEMENTED. **Active projects are AQUORA and KIRA-9 only.** This issue is the new active next-build scope, **not** permission to rewrite/publish the previous hotfix in parallel with another Work session.

## Radio exclusivity — owner requirement (Nov 5, 2026)
**AQUORA AIR sensing and BLE MIDI must NEVER run simultaneously or share the active Bluetooth radio.** These are mutually exclusive radio owners, regardless of whether the lower-level BLE stack could technically time-share. This policy overrides any earlier request to try concurrent AIR+BLE MIDI operation.

- Enabling **BLE MIDI** automatically turns **AIR OFF**, clears AIR signal/FX modulation state safely (smooth return to baseline, no abrupt wet/pitch discontinuity), releases AIR scanning/listener resources, and then starts BLE MIDI radio services.
- Enabling **AIR** automatically turns **BLE MIDI OFF**, sends safe Note Off/All Notes Off and disconnects/releases any BLE MIDI session (and stops wireless clock transmission) before AIR scanning begins. No stuck notes, ghost transport or leaked background radio tasks.
- UI shows one truthful active mode (AIR / BLE MIDI / RADIO OFF) with explicit transition feedback such as "AIR disabled for BT MIDI" or "BT MIDI disconnected for AIR"; do not silently activate both. Ensure settings toggles, Quick Find and physical controls all use the **same atomic radio-owner state machine**.
- On boot/restore, resolve impossible saved simultaneous-ON settings deterministically; only one radio owner starts. Avoid repeated forced scan/connect loops; document priority and provide a clear manual selection.
- **USB MIDI is not a Bluetooth radio consumer** and should continue functioning while AIR is active, subject to software/CPU/audio performance tests. Selecting AIR must not disable wired USB CoreMIDI connectivity, and selecting USB MIDI must not activate BLE MIDI.
- Test rapidly switching AIR→BLE→AIR (including during playback, at 16 voices and during connect/reconnect), safe fade and note flush, graceful disconnect, error recovery, CPU/audio deadlines and real radio states. Hardware RF behavior remains owner-unverified.

issues.title: P0: SAVE hangs on “Saving Bank” during PLAY; verify flash progress, fullscreen transition and recall
issues.body:
## Owner FM-1 hardware report — published v0.6.4 (2026-11-05)

**Symptom:** One-press SAVE sometimes takes an unexpectedly long time or remains visibly stuck on **“Saving Bank N”**. The text goes away after PLAY enters auto-fullscreen (about ten seconds). **This does not prove the bank was saved.** Owner has not yet verified a cold-boot recall of the affected bank. Record as a P0 data-integrity and live-performance concern.

### Source-grounded investigation

- `device/quicksave.c::arrangement_quick_save()` sets `quick_pending=1, bank_message=BANK_SAVING`, then `arrangement_service()` waits for `qread==qwrite` before taking a consistent snapshot. During a long stream of UI/control commands, this can defer starting the flash transaction.
- `arrangement_service()` calls `quick_poll()` once per `app_frame()`; it returns `1` while the asynchronous transaction is in progress. It changes to `BANK_SAVED` only after `quick_poll()==0`, which is intended to mean CRC/readback verification.
- On FM-1, `vendor/fm1-base/device/aquora_async_store.h::plat_aquora_save_poll()` returns `1` whenever `plat_cpu2_busy()`. Given the owner's visualizer freezes, worker fallback and high UI render costs (#26), investigate repeated worker-busy status and main-loop starvation. Also profile suspended flash erase/program/readback latency.
- `device/ui.c` displays a saving banner in band 4 while pending or started, and success/failure for three seconds after `quick_finished_ms`. `device/app.c` auto-enters fullscreen after 10 seconds on PLAY. Distinguish a **real save transaction still pending** from a stale/not-repainted saving banner or a fullscreen overlay that disappears without durable commit.
- Earlier isolated host storage/suspend regressions do **not** prove actual on-chip save latency or endurance when audio+heavy fullscreen visuals run.

### Required corrective behavior (urgent hotfix after verifying release ownership)

- [ ] Press SAVE once while stopped or **playing** on PLAY/SOUND/EVOLVE/MIX/DRUMS/SETUP/AIR or fullscreen; take a consistent snapshot promptly without blocking the audio deadline. Preserve the existing atomic alternating-sector CRC/readback transaction and power-cut safety.
- [ ] Show truthful, unambiguous progress: **Saving Bank N → Saved to Bank N** only after flash has committed/read back; **Save Failed / Retry** for errors; don't silently mask unfinished transactions after auto-fullscreen. Keep a small completion indicator when fullscreen is entered during an in-flight save.
- [ ] Record and expose request time, snapshot latency, flash initiation/erase/write/readback time, retries/suspend busy counts, timeout state and actual result. Add a bounded watchdog and explicit failure state to prevent indefinite “Saving…”; do NOT declare success merely when a timeout expires.
- [ ] Investigate audio/visual concurrency: `plat_cpu2_busy()` gating, fallback, `app_frame()` starvation, command-queue drain and platform `aq_flash_slice`; avoid new XRUN, latency or flash corruption. A save must not seize the audio callback or impede remaining visualization performance correction (#26).
- [ ] Verify saved **actual bank** after STOP and re-enter + after full reboot and reload, including patch IDs, mode, intention, eight-role arrangement, motion, FX, Nature AUTO/OFF/manual, exact reference settings, all four banks and repeated overwrite. Recover correctly from injected flash failures and power interruptions. Never overwrite another bank.
- [ ] Add deterministic host/emulator tests for playback under high UI load, continuous commands, both visualizers, fullscreen transition at ten seconds, worker busy/fallback, save then immediate load, flash faults and power-cycle rollback, with no UI false success.
- [ ] Update active queue and manual with expected honest save state. Preserve music modes, sound, all 4 banks, previously working v0.6.4 data and flashing rollback. Physical FM-1 acceptance requires owner testing.

**Status:** OPEN / suspected save-state starvation or redraw issue; specific cause still unproven. Release-blocking data integrity and UX defect. Coordinate with P0 [#26](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/issues/26), and do not race existing Work builds.

# P0 FM-1 v0.6.4 physical regression — visualizers freeze, audio lag, intro needs vibrant colored negative space

**Owner physical FM-1 report:** Both visualizers visibly freeze; owner now hears audio lag on published v0.6.4. Three owner-provided LCD photos capture genuine on-device metrics. **Do not publish the existing v0.6.5 intro-only candidate until this release-blocking performance issue is resolved.** Owner additionally requests a **bright, vibrant treatment for the unused/negative space of the dedicated intro**—not the normal visualizers.

## Physical evidence transcribed from screenshots

**PERFORMANCE 0.6.4 (screen 1):**
- PLAY BLITS FPS ×10: **174** → 17.4 frame blits/s, below nominal 20 target.
- MISSED /2s: **0** (does not exclude stutter / long individual draw calls).
- AUDIO MEAN: **4894 µs**, FX MEAN: **270 µs**, AUDIO+FX BUD: **88%**.
- DMA XRUN DELTA: **0** in that sampling window; **NOT proof** of no audible lag at other times.
- WORK: **6154 µs**, FALLBACK: **1**.

**CALLBACK/CORE (screen 2):**
- Audio callback block **256 frames / 5805 µs** at 44.1 kHz.
- Callback MEAN **5186 µs** (~89% budget), PEAK **5381 µs**, P95/P99 shown **5400 µs** (~93%). Near deadline, insufficient comfortable DSP headroom.
- GEOMETRY **6156 µs**; UI DRAW **58266 µs = 58.3 ms**, exceeding the nominal **50 ms / 20 FPS** frame interval; **16 active voices**, INPUT DROPS 0.

**VOICE INSPECTOR (screen 3):** voice slot 1/Lead, MIDI/AGE 73 ms, remain 0, note ON/OFF 161, GUARDS 1, SACRED ACTIVE Hz 55, FIXED ACTIVE Hz 0. The inspector alone is not proof of stuck notes, but useful for correlating stop/voice cleanup.

The photo readings are from distinct debug pages/windows; do not assume they are simultaneous or universal, and do not equate 0 XRUNs in one window with no glitches.

## Grounded v0.6.4 renderer source investigation

- `device/visual_worker.c::resonance_job()` recomputes a **25×25 nodal_field grid**, walks all **24×24 marching squares**, and appends up to **512 line segments**; `visual_job()` reports ~6 ms geometry on this FM-1.
- `device/ui.c::geometry()` loops **all node_count segments for each of five 48-pixel LCD bands**, with per-band clipping and line drawing; `draw(animate)` can take ~58 ms. Inspect actual segment count, per-band line/clipping, LCD blits, refresh cost and SPI/DMA constraints; don't guess which is dominant without profiling.
- `device/visual_worker.c::prepare_geometry()` calls `plat_cpu2_run`/`plat_cpu2_wait`; `worker_fallbacks=1` means at least one worker fallback occurred. Determine why (busy/late/bad core), and ensure core-0 cannot be swamped by synchronous geometry during playback. Do **not** assume core-1 permanently failed solely from count 1.
- `device/app.c` visual `FRAME_MIN_MS=50`, and the CPU-headroom guard only suppresses frames when callback P95 exceeds ~5500–5700 µs. Examine why frame pacing may stutter even when MISSED=0.
- Actual v0.6.4 `tests/corrective_previews.py` relies on static intro captures; separate intro fix at #24 / draft PR #25 restores a moving AQUORA-only intro, but it is **not performance accepted**.

## Mandatory next corrective release (coordinate with existing v0.6.5 PR #25)

- [ ] **Audio-first emergency gate:** profile default PLAY, both visualizers, full-screen on/off, a heavy 16-voice high-drum / Nature / FX / binaural case, mode/intention changes, and cold boot; measure callback mean/P95/P99, XRUN deltas and audio continuity on host native/emulator and owner hardware.
- [ ] Fix the **visualizer freeze and audio lag**, not merely hide metrics. Optimize nodal calculations and rendering complexity, prepare_geometry wait/fallback, band drawing, and/or adaptive workload scheduling with credible measured evidence. Avoid allocations, per-sample FFT, new expensive audio work, and unbounded synchronous geometry calls.
- [ ] **Render budget:** target ≥20 delivered FPS when audio headroom allows; if under pressure, gracefully reduce visual complexity/frame rate rather than sacrificing callback deadlines; never freeze indefinitely or leave stale images after transitions. Record benchmark frame-time distributions (not only averages), whether rendering and blits happen on core 0 or core 1, and whether fallback stays sticky.
- [ ] Force a **bounded and justified maximum geometry workload** even if the other core fails. Keep intro visualization entirely separate from music visualizers and keep both normal visualizers hidden during intro.
- [ ] Add targeted performance and visual regression tests to ensure (a) Original and Resonance Plate both keep moving while engine plays, (b) nonvisible views do no work, (c) no missed audio deadlines under representative maximum load, and (d) cold boot + fallback behave acceptably.
- [ ] **Intro appearance:** during the ~8-second skippable AQUORA wordmark/audio intro, make the formerly blank background/negative space a **bright, vibrant, intentionally composed themed color field**, with readable wordmark/version and visible lightweight standalone motion. Do **not** draw the normal Original or Resonance Plate visualizers, sacrifice text contrast, create full-screen per-pixel effects, or introduce measurable audio/UI latency. RGB565 precomputed flat fills / sparse accents only. Allow a clean transition to the user's chosen Black/White regular UI afterward. Check on both backgrounds and all themes.
- [ ] Keep v0.6.4 released bits immutable, preserve musical sound, three modes, freshly-selected intention patches, glide/vibrato, banks and site. Rebuild **v0.6.5** from latest verified checkpoint under exclusive lock, publish only after targeted+full acceptance and real GitHub/installer/site verification. Owner tests physically.

**Status:** observed hardware symptoms and concrete performance metrics confirmed from uploaded photos, root cause not yet proven; v0.6.5 performance correction and vibrant intro are **OPEN / release-blocking**. Related #12 #15 #17 #24 (PR #25).

**Owner request (November 5, 2026):** Add three selectable musical modes — **Standard, Cinematic, Neoclassical** — and automatically choose musically appropriate **lead and bass glide/vibrato** whenever intention or music mode changes. ## Music modes (distinct from Nature Character or EVOLVE Development)

- [ ] **STANDARD:** Preserve the widely liked existing v0.6.3 musical character as the default/backwards-compatible baseline: balanced generative eight-role ambient performance, intention-appropriate instruments and gentle rhythm. Not a random rename of existing Nature Style.
- [ ] **CINEMATIC:** Audible long-form soundtrack language: spacious drones and pads/choir/strings, expressive sustained leads, deep controlled bass, evolving harmonic swells, tasteful cinematic pulses/percussion and larger phrase/section arcs. Frequency/intention stays exact; avoid indiscriminately louder output or costly voices/FX.
- [ ] **NEOCLASSICAL:** Contemporary chamber/piano-centered language: expressive piano motifs/arpeggios, plucks/strings/woodwinds, tasteful melodic counterpoint, thoughtful harmonic progression, natural phrase dynamics and restrained gentle percussion/FX. Avoid simply muting drums and calling it Neoclassical.
- [ ] Each mode changes **musical composition and articulation**, not just a label, skin, tempo or volume: intention-aware curated patch weights per role, bass shapes, melodic/rhythmic grammar, voicings, drums, texture/Nature AUTO choices, FX balance, motion and evolution patterns. Preserve all 13 intention identities and per-intention exact reference Hz / binaural separation.
- [ ] Changing mode intentionally generates an appropriate **fresh, coherent musical realization**, consistent with owner rule that A→B→A intention changes must refresh unlocked patches, motifs and grooves rather than replay fixed presets. Preserve locks, manual Nature/OFF, Freeze where relevant, exact bank recalls and save-state semantics.
- [ ] Clear accessible **MUSIC MODE: STANDARD / CINEMATIC / NEOCLASSICAL** selection, directly editable from a sensible PLAY/SOUND/EVOLVE surface and Quick Find with visible current mode, control name and K1–K4 values. Don't conflate music mode with the current `nature_style` four-position Nature Character or `evolve_level` Stable/Subtle/Flowing/Adventurous. If these interact, define deterministic profile precedence and show it on device.
- [ ] Persist selected mode in full 4-bank SAVE/LOAD and any appropriate global default. Backward-compatible serialization/migration from v0.6.3 banks: **default STANDARD** without corrupting old banks or changing their stored sounds. Do not overwrite bank content merely on selection.

## Lead/bass glide + vibrato = intention × music mode auto-profile

- [ ] Provide intentional **automatic per-scene/per-mode motion defaults** for LEAD and BASS (`glide_mode`, `glide_ms`, `vibrato_rate`, `vibrato_depth`), using safe musical ranges. **Not every intention should have strong glide or vibrato**. Some Neoclassical lines may use little/no glide and restrained expressive vibrato; Cinematic sustained roles can use more expressive smooth motion; Standard retains familiar balance.
- [ ] Recompute and apply defaults on **every intention change and music-mode change** (including A→B→A). Do not let previous intention's accidental or auto-selected glide/vibrato values carry over. Ensure the effect is **audible and actually used by the synthesis engine**, not only the UI value changing.
- [ ] Preserve deliberate performer customization via an explicit **AUTO / MANUAL (override/lock)** concept for each supported role or motion group. In AUTO reapply intention+mode defaults; in MANUAL preserve player-chosen glide/vibrato across subsequent scene/mode changes until reset to AUTO. Define consistent precedence alongside existing patch locks and saved `sr_motion[2]` fields. Never silently overwrite explicitly locked settings.
- [ ] Expose selected lead/bass motion source (**AUTO profile** vs **MANUAL override**), current glide mode/time and vibrato depth/rate in live on-device control labels and Quick Find. Make switching back to AUTO discoverable.
- [ ] No pitch out of the selected intention's scale from glide/Play Along except intended smooth portamento between valid endpoints; prevent hanging notes, clicks or sudden giant pitch glides on live mode changes. Smooth/phase-safe reset where necessary, no per-sample new expensive DSP.

## Implementation facts from v0.6.3

- `device/dsp/engine.c::sr_set_scene()` already has a `static sr_motion intention_motion[SR_SCENES][2]` table and reassigns `e->motion[t]` for unlocked lead/bass. It has **no independent three-way MUSIC MODE state**, and scene changes don't currently separate manual motion override state. Current mode meaning should be augmented rather than duplicated.
- `device/dsp/serenity.h`: `sr_motion {glide_ms, glide_mode, vibrato_depth, vibrato_rate}`, `motion[2]`, `nature_style` (separate Nature Character).
- `device/app.c` motion controls 32–35 edit lead/bass values, while saved global `settings.motion[2]` and bank `arrangement.c` both contain motion data. Audit precedence/migration so user edits aren't lost or unintentionally reapplied.
- `device/arrangement.c` has an existing versioned/CRC bank record; add migration-safe mode and motion-override persistence without silently invalidating old bank CRCs or shrinking rollback safety.

## Required acceptance before marking complete

- [ ] **13 intentions × 3 music modes × multiple song seeds**, with A→B→A revisits in each: generate and verify actual 8-role note-event/patch/kit/texture differences while respecting locks, plus intended stable identity and exact reference frequencies.
- [ ] Level-matched **audible PCM previews** of all three modes using the *same* intention and comparable loudness; ensure composition/instrumentation differences are appreciable rather than cosmetic.
- [ ] Verify actual **lead/bass glide and vibrato settings** before/after changes for every intention × mode, appropriate low/zero choices, actual pitch/envelope DSP, AUTO→MANUAL→AUTO behavior, and scene/modal changes during playback with no stuck notes or glitches.
- [ ] Bank upgrade v0.6.3→v0.6.4, fresh save/restore/restart with all 3 modes + motion override, backward compatibility with older 4 banks, no regression to one-press SAVE.
- [ ] Profile heavy 16-voice + high-drums + stereo binaural + Nature + FX under mode changes; native/single-core/emulator host acceptance. Music quality and FM-1 delivery remain owner listening checks, never inferred from host alone.
- [ ] Update firmware manual, on-device navigation, the short v0.6.4 hotfix active queue and truthful release notes. Avoid modifying immutable v0.6.3 artifacts or making a new independent development session while one writer owns the build lock.

issues.title: P0: All 19 AQUORA drum kits sound muffled — restore crisp attacks and distinct timbre without regressions
issues.body:
## Actual FM-1 feedback — **ALL 19 DRUM KITS sound muffled**, not merely FM Moon Kit (v0.6.1)
The owner tested **every kit** and found similarly muffled/lacking attack/presence. Example: FM Moon Kit at **Density 8, HIT 95%, Level 100%** still sounds muffled. Do not limit the fix to that kit or assume high Density/HIT equals brightness/punch.

### Published v0.6.1 source evidence
- `device/dsp/engine.c::drum_sample()` uses exactly one shared kick, hand/snare and shaker architecture for **all 19 kits**. Kits change `kick, hand, shaker, root, skin, decay, brush`; FM kits (ID >=15) mostly switch a modest sine-based FM variant.
- Kick is dominated by a ~47–71Hz low-frequency sine with a small overtone and mostly slow natural-decay envelope. Hand transient is `tap*.64f + filtered_noise*.36f`; shaker uses high-passed noise. This architecture tends toward soft/dark timbres across *all* kits and may lack a sufficiently bright, transient attack layer, regardless of kit values.
- `drum_hit` is the probability of additional strikes on otherwise empty eligible subdivisions; **it does not increase per-hit attack/brightness**. `drum_density` controls placement/number of strikes; `drum_level` scales amplitude. The user expects higher punch/clarity, but these parameters do not supply that.
- Audio path includes user-level **Presence** only as a gain modifier (`1+(presence-50)*.006`), and global auto gain/auto level, a reverb/delay send, and master limiter. Trace **drum-specific frequency response, transients, routing, wet/dry, limiter gain reduction and gain staging** to identify other contributors to perceived muffling rather than presuming one specific cause.
- Keep low CPU cost: v0.6.1 initial flash default PLAY nearly 99% callback budget, later clean cold boot 83% Audio+FX and 0 XRUNs. No expensive FFT/reverb or multivoice sample playback without measurements.

### Mandatory remedies
1. Do **level-matched A/B analysis** for all 19 kits in isolation and in full generative mix, on headphones and onboard speaker where available. Render the kick, snare/hand and hats separately with spectral envelopes/attack times, transient peak/crest, masking, auto-level and limiting on/off, FX 0 vs normal. Find a shared bottleneck.
2. Retune shared kick/snare/hat DSP for noticeably clearer, stronger well-defined attack while preserving ambient softness: low-cost short noise/click onset, brighter and more natural snare/hand material, controlled high-frequency shimmer/hats, better multi-stage envelope / pitch sweep, more variety and separation between kits. Expose a **single DRUM TONE / BRIGHTNESS or PUNCH** parameter if needed (one canonical setting, directly labeled), separate from LEVEL, DENSITY and HIT.
3. Correct gain staging and masking with bass, piano, Nature and reverb. Don't just normalize/compress the entire mix louder or reduce all melodic sound. Preserve soft/high-dynamics presets; users should be able to make drums crisp when desired.
4. In DRUMS UI accurately explain and label **DENSITY = how many hits, HIT = optional-hit probability, LEVEL = volume, PRESENCE = drum mix emphasis**; don't pretend any of these is a brightness control. Add direct **per-kit audition** in context, and make kit differences obvious.
5. Add meaningful distinctiveness to all 19 kits, not variants of one muffled sine/noise mixture. Any new FM drum synthesis must be bounded and profiled per callback; preserve each existing kit name/ID and saved settings. When user selects FM Moon at 8/95/100, it must be audible and clear, not just louder or busier.
6. Compare per-kit and full-mix listening renders (old/new), transient and LUFS or equivalent level-matched playback, no clipping, no XRUN regression, 16 voice default-playback performance and long session. Owner physical-listening acceptance remains unverified until tested.
7. Preserve arrangement diversity, soft ambient intentions and ability to mute/solo; tests must cover across all 13 intentions and musical styles. No hidden extra per-sample processing when drums OFF.
8. Treat as release-blocking for next corrective version and retain rollback versions. 
Status: owner-observed all-kit issue, **not yet repaired**.

issues.title: NEXT BUILD P0: Visualizer 2 — Cymatics (ground-up water-and-sand redesign)
issues.body:
## Owner v0.6.1 hardware feedback — retain visual design, greatly deepen musical responsiveness
"The second visualizer looks cool now", is going in the right direction, but the owner wants it to **react dramatically and continuously to the actual audio, selected intention, musical content and tuned frequencies**, visually inspired by the Japanese water-crystal / Masaru Emoto imagery. Maintain angelic, peaceful, beautiful identity, volumetric/2.5D depth, strong screen fill and slight downward centering previously requested. **Preserve the working Polar Bloom look** and enhance it, rather than reverting to the rejected horizontal ribbons or starting over.

### Source finding, published v0.6.1
`device/visual_worker.c::resonance_job()` currently makes 8 rings ×33 points, with `petals=3u+vis_input.frequency/300u`, `scene` affecting colors primarily, `bass` changing radius, drums and piano modifying ripples, choir changing a swell, and each track's meter scaling an amplitude. `device/ui.c::geometry()` draws ring connections with modest visual motion and color mainly selected by role. It reacts somewhat, but **intentions are not driving distinct evolving visual structure** and reference frequency only coarsely changes petals. This is not a rich audio-driven geometry generator. Also correct the Polar-only PLAY UI disappearing bug tracked in #14.

### Required design — artistic cymatics-inspired, not asserted scientific proof
- Treat Emoto-style water-crystal images as **visual inspiration**, not evidence that intention/frequencies scientifically change water or provide medical healing.
- **13 intention-specific coherent geometry/behavior profiles:** distinct symmetry, petal structure, branching, fractal-like crystalline lines, ripple propagation, mesh curvature, depth/tilt and color moods. Selecting a new intention must produce a visibly different yet coherent motif. Avoid cheap random geometric reshuffles; maintain beautiful stable motifs with gradual transitions.
- **Frequency-to-form mapping:** known selected Hz and 432/440 mode drive safe bounded phase/symmetry/interference/tension/halo characteristics. Ensure changing an actual frequency changes geometry deterministically, does not alias violently, and respects precise audio tuning. Frequency is an artistic mapping; no medical claims.
- **Real-time audio-driven modulation with clearly separable features:** bass and kick energize low-radius pulses/core/height; drum onsets send fast expanding ripples and spark points; piano/plucks articulate fine structures and harmonic flicker; pads/choir slowly expand/smooth petals and luminous halos; melodic pitch/motif/chord motion changes resonance/symmetry/rotation in a controlled musical fashion. Use real role meters, onset/event counters and cheap precomputed pitch/event metadata, or bounded aggregate envelope/band features when available. Don't fabricate FFT bins or expensive spectral capture.
- Add visible **attack → bloom → sustain → decay**; movement should respond to notes quickly yet retain graceful decay and naturally evolve as arrangement/intentions change. Distinguish genuinely audible onset/quiet/silence.
- Optional easy-to-find **REACTIVITY, COMPLEXITY and DEPTH** controls with safe presets (Calm / Dynamic) if performance allows. Control level sensitivity, response curve and visual density without altering audio. No duplicate/conflicting visual controls.
- Fullscreen remains edge-to-edge 240x240 with slight vertically lowered focus; PLAY embedded preview maintains complete controls for BOTH visualizers. Intro uses saved visualizer/theme preferences (#16).
- **Very strict audio stability priority:** v0.6.1 default PLAY already near 99% callback budget, 82 XRUNs/2s (#12). Audio feature telemetry must be cheap control-rate snapshots; no per-audio-sample FFT/per-pixel glow/expensive sin() or allocations in audio ISR; geometry only while visible per #15; reuse LUT, fixed bounded vertices, row stripes, no hidden worker dispatch. Simplify when CPU load is high rather than sacrificing audio stability.
- Test every intention and frequency in deterministic snapshots with representative audio note events; prove geometry really changes for intention/frequency and amplitude/onsets/motif; verify silence behaves correctly; A/B clips for dry/active 16-voice arrangement and no hidden CPU work. Native/single-core/emulator and physical delivered FPS + beauty verified by owner.
- Keep exact previous selection, settings migration and original visualizer unaffected. Complete next versioned corrective release once performance/audio are stable; not a cosmetic mock-up.

**Status: requested, not implemented; release-blocking to owner acceptance after default playback stability.**

## Official visualizer name — owner directive (2026-11-06)

**Visualizer 2's official name in the next AQUORA build is `Cymatics`.** The current public v0.6.5 on-device label `Resonance Plate` is legacy; replace it with **Cymatics** consistently in the actual firmware's visualizer selector, UI headings/knob labels and any relevant references, while implementing the substantive ground-up water/sand cymatics visualization specified in this issue. **Do not count a label-only change as completing the redesign.**

**Visualizer 1 remains `Original`**, with its existing non-water visual identity preserved or restored under Issue #33. Only Visualizer 2 is intended to resemble water/sand. Keep existing saved visualizer selection compatible through the upgrade. Test visible naming and selection in 240×240 screens, firmware/emulator, settings save/recall, and owner hardware confirmation. This is next-build scope, not yet implemented; leave v0.6.5 unchanged.

issues.title: P1: Persist selected visualizer for startup intro; ultra-lightweight refreshed UI with vibrant selectable themes
issues.body:
## Owner request — corrective build after v0.6.1
1. **Remember which visualizer was selected** across power cycles and make AQUORA's ~10-second startup introduction display/animate **that selected visualizer**, not hardcoded Original. Both Original and Polar Bloom must work; future presets should use the same saved selection system.
2. Give the entire AQUORA UI a noticeably more polished, **extremely lightweight** visual appearance, with a few **distinct vibrant color themes**. Never add expensive layers, shaders, blur or background UI animation merely to change colors. Preserve the immediate editing/navigation fixes and audio stability.

## Confirmed source gaps (published v0.6.1)
- `device/app.c` persists only `motion[2]`, `perfect_key`, `lighting`, and `fps_auto` in `aq_settings` (`version=0x41513032`). **Visualizer selection is not globally saved**.
- `device/arrangement.c` includes `record->visual=visual_mode` for *individual arrangement banks*, but `arrangement_init()` resets `visual_mode=0` on startup. Loading a bank can restore it; ordinary selection followed by power cycling cannot be relied on to persist.
- `device/ui.c` intro calls `geometry(band*48)`, which is driven by the same `vis_output`; `visual_worker.c::prepare_geometry()` uses `visual_mode` for its variant. The persisted selection must be restored **before** the first intro geometry/paint.
- `device/ui.c` uses many hardcoded `RGB(...)` values and `static const uint16_t colors[SR_TRACKS]`. Refactor to **precomputed 16-bit RGB565 theme palettes**, not runtime per-pixel hue calculations.

## Implementation / UI design
### A. Persist and use visualizer choice
- Global **visualizer preference** changes when selected; persists without requiring a manual SAVE or bank save. Load it before `app_ui_init()` renders any intro/preview frame.
- Intro must render the **last selected Original or Polar Bloom** and use the saved UI theme; optional music-reactive dynamics can work where audio actually exists, but a silent intro must not need fake FFT/extra audio.
- Keep distinct **arrangement-bank visual** behavior predictable: define whether bank-load switches the active visualizer (currently recorded) and synchronize the global preference correctly; do not inadvertently replace a user's global selection when loading unrelated data unless explicitly chosen. Document visible semantics.
- Use one versioned, compact settings schema that migrates old v0.6.0/v0.6.1 settings without losing saved LED mode, motion, perfect-key, FPS, banks. Range-check unknown/corrupt values; safe fallback Original/legacy theme. Ensure atomic/low-wear writes or save-on-change/debounced/power-down mechanism appropriate to flash. No per-frame writes.
- Intro remains ~10s and instantly skippable on any knob/button/key without changing a setting or playing a surprise note. Preserve safe startup audio level and battery overlay behavior.

### B. Extremely lightweight UI refresh
- Introduce 3–4 selectable, vivid but readable **static RGB565 palettes**, plus existing AQUORA/Legacy styling. Suggested: **Aurora** (teal/violet), **Neon Lagoon** (cyan/magenta), **Solar Bloom** (coral/gold), **Midnight Prism** (indigo/electric blue). Final names/colors may be tuned for 240×240 screen visibility; user should perceive meaningful differences.
- Apply them consistently to main interface backgrounds, high-contrast text, knob focus/selection accents, SOUND and EVOLVE graphs, mixer meters and visualizer coloring/lighting accents as appropriate. Maintain track-role identity and mute/solo indicators. Theme should not change audio or nature/FX parameters.
- Prefer a **single canonical** `SETUP > DISPLAY > THEME` control and direct Quick Find entry. Avoid duplicate theme/edit controls in unrelated pages; UI shortcuts must point to the same setting.
- Make the whole UI easier to read and edit: crisp labels, clear selection highlight, comprehensible K1–K4 values, predictable navigation, minimal chrome and visual clutter, smooth but **event-driven** updates. This is a lightweight **visual design system**, not a heavyweight new UI framework.

issues.title: P0 real-time performance: zero hidden visualization/graph DSP and rendering workload
issues.body:
## Owner mandatory performance directive
**Whenever a visualizer, animation or real-time SOUND/EVOLVE graph is not actually visible, it must consume no ongoing rendering/geometry/telemetry processing resources.** A single cheap active-view conditional is acceptable; the continuous hidden work is not. In the current physical v0.6.1 the audio budget is ~97–99% with frequent XRUNs, so this is P0.

### Verified 0.6.1 behavior to audit
- `device/app.c::app_frame` animates on `intro_active||page==PAGE_PLAY||page==PAGE_MIX||page==PAGE_SOUND||page==PAGE_EVOLVE` at ~20 fps even if visible page content is static or the SOUND category picker is on. Ensure **content visibility**, not page membership alone, controls animation.
- It correctly calls `prepare_geometry()` only on PLAY, but `device/ui.c::draw` can render the old `geometry` from other page fallbacks, sometimes for no useful reason. Review why/when visualizer geometry is required.
- `scope_track` changes to `SR_TRACKS` outside SOUND > Instrument graph, and `engine.c::render_samples` checks `scope_track<SR_TRACKS` before decimated capture. Keep this skip and optimize hot path so non-viewing avoids capture math/copies entirely (do not retain per-voice graph accumulation).
- `app_frame` unconditionally advances `evolve_history[64]` whenever transport steps change, even when EVOLVE graph isn't visible; this may be cheap but owner requests no continuous hidden graph bookkeeping; gate unless event history is required by musical engine. Do not disable **musical evolution** itself, which must continue sounding even when EVOLVE page is hidden.
- App init unconditionally calls `visual_init()`, `plat_cpu2_set(1)`; determine if worker can park safely when no visualizer graph is needed, without breaking audio or destabilizing core startup. No CPU2 worker dispatch or geometry while hidden; no hidden LCD rendering/blits.
- AIR radio/control, the main generative engine, its role meters for limiter/UX, LED output and audio effects must **not be turned off merely because their UI widgets are hidden**. Separate *audio-critical data* from optional visualization-only telemetry.

### Required implementation
1. One authoritative **visibility/consumer activation map**: intro visualization, PLAY embedded/fullscreen Original/new flagship, SOUND waveform/envelope/FX view, EVOLVE timeline, MIX meters, AIR sensor meter, debug/performance, hidden/static/setup. Only visible (and needed) modules may schedule graph/visual work; switching focus/picker/debug/fullscreen must update gates before next callback/render.
2. When a widget becomes hidden, immediately suspend its: geometry updates, graph sample capture, analysis/spectrum/band computations, per-frame animations/timers, ring-buffer/history writes for purely visual telemetry, worker submissions/waits, LCD strip blits and dirty-redraw requests. Keep minimal state needed for correct restoration only.
3. Sound engine and musical section evolution keep running regardless of UI view. Re-enable visual telemetry gracefully upon return without stale samples/ghosts. Respect fades on exit and full-screen battery fade; avoid stranded overlays, interrupt races and audio glitches.
4. Implement compiled/host counters for each module: **geometry jobs**, **graph samples captured**, **EVOLVE history updates**, **UI rendered frames and blits**, **CPU2 jobs/waits**, **inactive per-frame processing**, **audio/FX timing**. In hidden-state soak tests, optional graphics/telemetry counters must remain ZERO (except one-time transitions), and no visual-only DSP work in the 44.1 kHz callback.
5. Compare audio callback mean/p95/p99/max and XRUN delta at identical stimuli with each graphic mode ACTIVE vs HIDDEN, including SOUND picker, EVOLVE off-screen, FULLSCREEN on/off, debug, display static and different page transitions. Target measurable reduction and no 16-voice crackle; do not infer delivered FPS from submitted blits.
6. Keep animations attractive and responsive **when actually visible** at optimized bounded rates. Allow static screen to redraw only when state/values change; no pointless 20 fps animation. Use dirty 240×48 strips where practical. No avoidable background CPU/GPU/radio work.
7. All state cleanup/visibility transition tests, native and forced single-core, host emulator, audio regression, actual FM1 performance evidence owner verified. Don't fake gains by suppressing XRUN metrics or degrading sound.

### Release
Cross-reference #7 full optimization and new v0.6.1 hardware performance issue. Record as a hard P0 gate for next corrective firmware release; preserve v0.6.1 and previous rollbacks, don't alter a concurrent Work publisher. No implementation/passed claim until source, tests and artifacts exist.

issues.title: P1 late-add 0.6.1: compact battery status indicator with automatic fullscreen fade-out
issues.body:
## Owner directive — add to the currently in-progress corrective build (late integration)
Add a **small, readable battery meter/status icon** throughout AQUORA's normal interface. In fullscreen, it should be briefly visible then **fade away completely**, leaving the music visualizer immersive and truly edge-to-edge (see #10). This is a compact, bounded, low-risk late addition **before the final integration tests and release**, not a reason to redo completed work.

### Verified existing platform API
FM1-base `include/plat.h` defines `int plat_battery(void)` with values:
- `-1`: battery state not yet read;
- `0..3`: coarse battery level, from empty to full;
- `4`: powered by USB host (not proof battery is charging).

The published 0.6.0 `device/ui.c` has no `plat_battery` display, and its fullscreen path renders `geometry(band*48)` across all five 240×48 strips. Integrate a tiny icon/status overlay into the existing strip UI path without changing or delaying the audio engine. Do **not** invent a high-precision battery percentage from a 4-step reading.

### User-visible behavior
1. Normal mode: show a compact, attractive battery glyph (four possible levels) in a consistent small top corner where it does not obstruct active controls, with a clear low-battery indicator and a distinct **USB powered** glyph when `plat_battery()==4`.
2. Unknown (`-1`): show a neutral/unknown icon or temporarily omit; never report 0%, charge state, or failure falsely. Avoid displaying spurious battery level during ADC settling.
3. Fullscreen: selected visualizer still fills the entire 240×240 LCD. Battery indicator may appear discreetly for a moment after fullscreen entry, then fade via a short nonblocking 1–3 second stepped-dim transition to **fully invisible** (no persistent blank overlay, header or ghost pixels). Never shrink or letterbox the visualizer to reserve icon space.
4. Low battery: if a supported, trusted status is detected, allow a brief unobtrusive warning/reappearance; do not repeatedly cover the artwork or make unsupported claims about numeric remaining time/percent. If stronger critical warnings are desired, derive reliable capabilities from the hardware driver first.
5. Consistent behavior on PLAY/SOUND/EVOLVE/MIX/DRUMS/SETUP/AIR, menu navigation, enter/exit fullscreen, wake gestures and 10-second auto fullscreen. Don't consume playable keyboard events or alter settings/transport.
6. Poll battery at a bounded UI/control rate only, not inside the audio callback; avoid interfering with key ADC scanning. Re-render only on status/fade changes. Implement fade using inexpensive color palette steps or bounded dithering, not costly per-pixel alpha shaders.
7. Make battery status accessible from a readable status/ABOUT area if the icon would otherwise be ambiguous.

### Acceptance
- Host UI tests for -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4; low/USB state; fullscreen fade sequence; return from fullscreen; no stale pixels or permanent obscuring of edge-to-edge artwork.
- Actual 240×240 normal and fullscreen screenshots (e.g. at entry and 3 seconds later), correct small icon, clean fade and full-screen art occupancy.
- Build/test native + single-core + emulator after integration; compare audio and FPS behavior against current branch; zero audio/FX processing change.
- User verifies physical battery state and LCD behavior on FM-1; not hardware-verified by host tests.

### Concurrent-build safety
AQUORA 0.6.1 development may be underway in another Work environment. **Do not edit shared in-progress source from a separate concurrent worker, replace tags, force-push, or publish from two environments.** The **single active release builder** should read this issue, implement it near final UI integration, and include it in the 0.6.1 final acceptance matrix. Preserve v0.6.0 and rollback.

Status: **Requested / not yet implemented**.

These restricted coordinate ranges help explain why a fullscreen mode can technically draw all bands while the actual visual doesn't use the screen's height/edges.
- [`device/app.c`](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/blob/v0.6.0/device/app.c) automatically enters fullscreen after 10s PLAY inactivity; knob/button activity exits it, while keys can still play. Preserve these behaviors unless changed by owner.

Center main focus visually around ~(120,120), with meaningful details across the full area. Adapt scaling to both Original and Vizz-inspired Mesh Flow / Polar Bloom etc, without rendering off-screen or wasting CPU.
3. The Vizz-inspired mode must be genuinely distinct from the rejected eight horizontal ribbons; no simple reskin. Audio-reactive bass/drums/piano/pads/choir modulation with smoothing and intention-aware palette, gentle beautiful motion even in quiet passages.
4. Preserve automatic fullscreen after 10s of inactivity on PLAY, selected look, direct exit by deliberate UI interaction without accidentally altering sound/transport, and keys continuing to play without unwanted fullscreen dismissal. Allow a clearly documented quick exit or transient overlay only when requested.
5. Progressive rendering and safe clipping: efficient 240×48 LCD strip draw, fixed vertex/particle budgets, correct coordinate transforms, no bands/tearing artifacts, no stale pixels after entering/exiting or selecting presets. Do not add costly per-pixel glow/FFT; optimize along with issue #7.
6. Provide true **240×240 stills and short emulator clips** for Original vs new second visualizer, embedded PLAY vs fullscreen, quiet vs full arrangement, showing composition occupies the frame. Software verify bounds, frame update coverage, geometry clipping and UI absence; owner verifies delivered LCD FPS and visual appeal on physical FM-1.
7. Do not modify published v0.6.0; implement for the next versioned corrective firmware.
